meta.title: PN junction from device physics (Poisson + drift-diffusion)
meta.tools: Nonlinear Poisson–Boltzmann solver (Newton), minority-carrier diffusion solver (finite differences)
meta.summary: Solve Poisson's equation self-consistently across a silicon p-n junction to get the built-in potential, depletion width and field, then solve minority-carrier diffusion to build the forward I–V curve; compare with the depletion approximation and the Shockley diode law.
meta.problem: The diode equation I = I_s(e^{V/V_T} − 1) is usually just given. Derive it — and its limits — from the physics of electrons and holes.
meta.theory:
Built-in potential $V_{bi}=V_T\ln\frac{N_AN_D}{n_i^2}$; depletion approximation: $W=\sqrt{\frac{2\varepsilon(V_{bi}-V)}{q}\frac{N_A+N_D}{N_AN_D}}$, peak field
$E_{max}=2(V_{bi}-V)/W$. Long-base diode: $I_s=qAn_i^2\left(\frac{D_n}{L_nN_A}+\frac{D_p}{L_pN_D}\right)$, ideality 1.
meta.method:
Si, T = 300 K, N_A = 10¹⁶, N_D = 10¹⁷ cm⁻³, n_i = 9.65×10⁹ cm⁻³, μ_n = 1350, μ_p = 480 cm²/Vs, τ = 1 µs, A = 1 mm². Equilibrium: Poisson with
Boltzmann carriers on a 2,000-point graded grid over 20 µm, Newton iteration. Bias: minority-carrier diffusion equation in each neutral region
solved numerically with law-of-the-junction boundary values, currents summed; compared with Shockley.

rows.quantity: Depletion width (depletion approximation vs 50 % carrier criterion)
